title: Halting bound for the guess-and-run machine
statement: Let $P$ and $Q$ be deterministic machines with $k$ Boolean work tapes, let $j$ be one of those tapes, and choose states $p_{\mathrm{exit}}$ of $P$ and $q_{\mathrm{entry}},q_{\mathrm{acc}},q_{\mathrm{rej}}$ of $Q$. Suppose that on input $z$, machine $P$ reaches configuration $c_P$ after $T_P$ steps, with state $p_{\mathrm{exit}}$, and does not visit that state at any earlier time. Suppose tape $j$ in $c_P$ has a block of at least $m$ nonblank cells beginning at its head position, followed by a blank cell, and that the cell immediately to the left of the head is blank. If, for every Boolean word $s$ of length $m$, machine $Q$ started from the configuration obtained by placing $s$ on tape $j$ at the head position of $c_P$ and entering state $q_{\mathrm{entry}}$ reaches either $q_{\mathrm{acc}}$ or $q_{\mathrm{rej}}$ within at most $T$ steps, with neither verdict visited earlier, then the nondeterministic machine that runs $P$, guesses and writes a bounded block, rewinds, and then runs $Q$ halts on every choice-bit word of length $T_P+2m+T+11$.
hypotheses_covered: $P,Q$ are deterministic machines with $k$ Boolean work tapes
$T_P$ is a natural number and $c_P$ is a configuration of $P$ on Boolean input $z$
$P$ run from its initial configuration for $T_P$ steps equals $c_P$
For some natural number $m$, the next $m$ cells of tape $j$ from its head are nonblank
The cell at head position plus $m$ is blank
The cell one position left of the tape head is blank
For every Boolean word of length $m$, the corresponding $Q$ run reaches acceptance or rejection by some time at most $T$
Before that verdict time, the $Q$ run has visited neither verdict state
